exercises.title: Dynamic Keyword Calls

theory.explanation: Run Keyword allows you to execute keywords dynamically by name stored in variables. This enables runtime decision-making about which keyword to execute, making your tests more flexible and adaptable to different scenarios.
theory.useCase: Useful for conditional execution, plugin systems, or when keyword names are determined at runtime based on configuration or test data.

task.description: Use Run Keyword to call keywords dynamically by name.
instructions: Use 'Run Keyword' to call the keyword stored in ${keyword_name}
The test should log the message

code.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Call
    # Write code here
code.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Dynamic Call
    ${keyword_name}    Set Variable    Log
    Run Keyword    ${keyword_name}    Dynamic execution!

hints: Run Keyword executes a keyword by name
First argument is the keyword name
Remaining arguments are passed to the keyword
Useful for conditional execution

exercises.title: Conditional Keyword Execution

theory.explanation: Run Keyword If conditionally executes a keyword based on a boolean expression. It's an alternative to IF...END blocks for simple conditional logic, allowing inline conditional execution.
theory.syntax: Run Keyword If    condition    Keyword Name    arg1    arg2
theory.useCase: Best for simple, single-line conditional keyword execution. For complex conditions or multiple statements, use IF...END blocks instead.

task.description: Use Run Keyword If to conditionally execute keywords.
instructions: Use 'Run Keyword If' to check if ${status} == 'active'
Use Run Keyword If    '${status}' == 'active'    Log    System is active

code.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
Conditional Execution
    # Write code here
code.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Conditional Execution
    ${status}    Set Variable    active
    Run Keyword If    '${status}' == 'active'    Log    System is active

hints: Run Keyword If takes condition and keyword
Condition must be in quotes for strings
Alternative to IF...END for simple cases
Can use ELSE with Run Keyword Unless

exercises.title: Keyword with Timeout

theory.explanation: The [Timeout] setting prevents keywords from running longer than a specified duration. If the timeout is exceeded, the keyword fails immediately. This is crucial for handling slow operations and preventing tests from hanging indefinitely.
theory.useCase: Essential for keywords that perform network operations, database queries, or any operation that might hang. Ensures tests fail fast rather than waiting indefinitely.

code.initialCode:
*** Test Cases ***
Test Timeout
    # Call keyword

*** Keywords ***
# Define keyword with timeout
code.solution:
*** Test Cases ***
Test Timeout
    Slow Operation

*** Keywords ***
Slow Operation
    [Timeout]    3 seconds
    Sleep    1s
    Log    Operation completed

hints: [Timeout] prevents keyword from running too long
Place after keyword name, before other settings
Keyword fails if timeout exceeded
Can use: seconds, minutes, hours

exercises.title: Keyword with Default Arguments

theory.explanation: Keywords can define default values for arguments using the syntax ${arg}=default_value. This makes keywords flexible and reusable by allowing callers to provide only the arguments they need to override, while other arguments use sensible defaults.
theory.useCase: Creates flexible APIs for keywords. Common in connection keywords (default host/port), configuration keywords (default settings), or any keyword where some parameters rarely change.

task.description: Create keywords with multiple default argument values.
instructions: Call it three ways: no args, with host, with host and port

*** Keywords ***
Connect To Server

hints: Multiple defaults: ${arg1}=val1 ${arg2}=val2
Can provide 0 to N arguments
Defaults filled from left to right
Makes keywords flexible and reusable

exercises.title: Variable Arguments (Varargs)

theory.explanation: The @{args} syntax allows keywords to accept any number of arguments. All provided arguments are collected into a list that can be iterated over. This creates highly flexible keyword interfaces similar to *args in Python.
theory.useCase: Perfect for keywords that process collections, batch operations, or logging utilities. Can be combined with regular arguments: ${required} ${optional}=default @{rest}
